question: How does the World Health Organization define an unsafe abortion?

options.A: A termination done by unskilled persons or in unsterile environments
options.B: A surgical procedure performed strictly in a teaching hospital
options.C: Any termination of pregnancy requested by a minor
options.D: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally before the twentieth week

explanation: You've got this! An unsafe abortion simply means a procedure done without proper medical skills, sterile tools, or safe standards. Always look out for the setting and who is performing it. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h1)

question: Why do many young women in Nigeria turn to secret, unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Advise from community health extension workers
options.B: Preference for traditional herbal preparations over modern medicine
options.C: Fear of social stigma and strict legal or religious restrictions
options.D: Lack of awareness that government hospitals offer free services

explanation: Societal pressure, shame, and strict laws often push frightened individuals away from safe hospitals and into risky, hidden places. A supportive nurse makes all the difference! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h1)

question: In Nigeria, under what single main condition is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: If fetal abnormalities are detected early
options.B: When requested by the parents of a minor
options.C: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.D: If the pregnancy resulted from financial hardship

explanation: Good to know for your exams and practice: Nigerian law is very strict and only permits abortion if it is done to preserve the mother's physical life. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h2)

question: How does Nigeria's strict legal stance on abortion end up hurting maternal health?

options.A: It forces procedures underground, leading to dangerous and secretive practices
options.B: It eliminates the need for contraceptives in rural communities
options.C: It guarantees that all women receive free post-abortion medications
options.D: It encourages traditional birth attendants to learn modern surgery

explanation: Making laws strict doesn't stop abortions; it just drives them underground where unsterile tools and secret methods cause severe complications. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h2)

question: What is a major root cause of unwanted pregnancies that lead to unsafe abortions?

options.A: Universal access to emergency birth control pills
options.B: Unmet needs and lack of access to modern contraceptives
options.C: Mandatory sex education classes in all primary schools
options.D: Excessive availability of free family planning clinics

explanation: When people cannot get or afford reliable birth control, unplanned pregnancies happen more often. Patient education is our best tool here! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h3)

question: A university student hides her pregnancy out of fear of expulsion and shame. What factor does this highlight?

options.A: A recognized legal indication for safe abortion
options.B: The direct physical effect of herbal toxins

explanation: Fear of judgment and losing her education often pushes a student toward risky, secret procedures. Empathy from nurses is crucial! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h3)

question: Which complication happens most directly when sharp metal objects are pushed into the uterus?

options.D: Renal stone formation and bladder spasms

explanation: Unskilled hands using sharp instruments can easily pierce the muscular wall of the uterus, causing heavy internal bleeding. That's a major medical emergency! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h4)

question: Why is washing out the vagina with harsh chemicals like bleach extremely dangerous?

options.A: It immediately halts all hormonal activity in the pituitary gland
options.B: It permanently prevents future urinary tract infections
options.C: It reliably evacuates the entire uterine contents within minutes
options.D: It causes severe chemical burns, tissue necrosis, and systemic toxicity

explanation: Caustic substances destroy delicate vaginal and cervical tissue right on contact and can enter the bloodstream, causing whole-body poisoning. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h4)

question: Which group of symptoms strongly points to a pelvic infection (sepsis) after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Painless vaginal bleeding and elevated blood pressure
options.B: High fever, foul-smelling discharge, and lower abdominal pain
options.C: Frequent urination, clear discharge, and normal temperature
options.D: Severe headache, blurred vision, and dry skin

explanation: Think of infection signs: fever, bad-smelling discharge, and tummy pain are classic red flags that unsterile instruments or tissue were left behind. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h5)

question: A young woman comes to the clinic with a rigid, painful abdomen and shoulder pain after visiting an unlicensed place. What is the most likely issue?
explanation: A board-like, rigid tummy and shoulder pain mean internal bleeding is irritating the lining of the abdomen (peritoneum). This needs urgent surgical care! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h5)

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse must do when a patient arrives with complications from an unsafe abortion?

options.B: Filling out legal police reports immediately
options.C: Conducting a detailed religious counseling session
options.D: Interrogating the patient about who performed the procedure

explanation: ABC comes first in every emergency! Saving the patient's life and treating shock always takes priority over asking questions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h6)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to communicate without judgment when assessing these patients?

options.A: It prevents the hospital from paying for laboratory investigations
options.B: It encourages the patient to truthfully share what methods were used, aiding proper treatment
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never experience physical pain
options.D: It is required by criminal law enforcement agencies in all Nigerian states

explanation: When patients feel judged, they hide details like chemical use or instrument trauma. A warm, welcoming attitude saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h6)

question: What is the preferred modern method for clearing the uterus safely during post-abortion care?
explanation: MVA is gentle, quick, and much safer for the uterine wall than old-fashioned sharp scraping (curettage). It's a wonderful modern standard! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h7)

question: Why must broad-spectrum antibiotics be given right away to a patient with a septic incomplete abortion?

options.A: To directly stimulate uterine contractions and expel retained tissue
options.B: To control and prevent the spread of ascending bacterial infection and septic shock
options.C: To replace lost blood volume and increase hemoglobin levels
options.D: To lower systemic blood pressure and reduce anxiety

explanation: Unsterile procedures let bacteria into the uterus, which can quickly spread into the blood and cause deadly septic shock. Quick antibiotics are life-savers! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h7)

question: How soon can a woman start ovulating and get pregnant again after an abortion?

options.A: Only after six months of complete amenorrhea
options.B: After her third normal menstrual cycle
options.D: As early as two weeks post-abortion

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! That is why family planning counseling before discharge is a vital part of nursing care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h8)

question: What is the main goal of giving birth control counseling during Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: To prevent repeat unintended pregnancies and subsequent unsafe abortions
options.B: To enforce government population control quotas in rural areas
options.C: To punish the patient for engaging in premarital sex
options.D: To permanently sterilize high-risk young women

explanation: PAC counseling is all about empowering women with choices so they can protect their health and avoid future unplanned pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h8)

question: How can community health nurses help lower the number of unsafe abortions?

options.A: By dispelling contraceptive myths and promoting youth-friendly reproductive health services
options.B: By teaching women how to safely use herbal concoctions at home
options.C: By arresting individuals who perform illegal abortions in local villages
options.D: By distributing heavy surgical instruments to traditional birth attendants

explanation: Education and open access to family planning stop unwanted pregnancies before they happen—that is the most powerful prevention! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h9)

question: A community health nurse notices many teens in her local area know nothing about birth control. What is her best first step?

options.A: Report all teenagers to the local police division for investigation
options.B: Establish an educational youth-friendly reproductive health club at the local center
options.C: Wait until patients present with complications before offering advice
options.D: Ban all public discussions regarding sexual health in schools

explanation: Creating safe, welcoming spaces gives adolescents the accurate facts they need to protect their health and futures. Great nursing initiative! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h9)
